Restrictions on POVMs

Memory, Locality, and Magic Constraints

← Back to Index

1 Restriction on POVMs

In practical quantum information processing, measurements are often subject to various constraints. We formalize these constraints by specifying a restricted set of allowed POVMs: \mathcal{M} = \{\{F_s\} \mid \{F_s\} \text{ satisfies the restriction}\}.

In general, we can store c copies of an identical state \rho^{\otimes c} and implement a c-replica measurement. Such a strategy is specified by a set of POVM operators \{F_s \in \mathrm{Herm}(d^c)\}_{s \in \mathcal{S}}, where s \in \mathcal{S} denotes the measurement outcome and the operators satisfy F_s \geq 0 and \sum_s {F_s} = \mathbb{I}(d)^{\otimes c}.

A key simplification is that we can always restrict to rank-1 POVMs without loss of generality, since arbitrary POVMs can be simulated by rank-1 POVMs through classical post-processing.

ImportantLemma

Any POVM \{F_s\}_s can be simulated through rank-1 POVM \{w_{sp}\cdot\ket{\psi_{sp}}\!\bra{\psi_{sp}}\}_{sp} by classical post-grouping \ket{\psi_{sp}}\!\bra{\psi_{sp}} \to F_s.

NoteProof (Click to expand)

Proof. Do Cholesky decomposition. Trivial. ◻

This equivalence means that given an arbitrary state \rho, the classical distribution generated by \{w_{sp}\cdot\ket{\psi_{sp}}\!\bra{\psi_{sp}}\}_{sp} is a coarse graining of that of \{F_s\}_s. Using Lemma, we conclude that it is sufficient to consider rank-1 POVMs only.

Based on different experiment restriction, F_s might only supports on a subset of space \mathrm{Herm}(d^c). Here below we characterized some typical restriction.

1.1 Memory-Limited Strategies

We first focus on the k-memory c-replica strategies. It is a c-replica measurement but with finite quantum-storage, as formally defined below.

NoteDefinition

A (c,k) adaptive strategy repeats T rounds of sampling. Within each round, as shown in the process diagram below, it repeatedly adds new copies of n-qubits \rho to the k-qubits memory \sigma^{(i)} and adaptively implements n+k \to k qubits POVMs \{M_s^{u}\}. \begin{align} \label{eq:procc_diag} \left[\rho \xrightarrow{\{M_{s_1}\}} \sigma^{(1)} \xrightarrow{\text{Add } \rho} \rho \otimes \sigma^{(1)}\xrightarrow{\{M_{s_1,s_2}\}} \sigma^{(2)} \xrightarrow{\text{Add } \rho} \cdots \rho \otimes \sigma^{(c)}\xrightarrow{\{M_{s_1,\cdots,s_c}\}} R_r \right]_{\times T} \end{align}

At the end of each round in a (c,k)-adaptive strategy, we get the result s_1,s_2,\cdots,s_c, corresponding to the POVM branch \begin{aligned} &\{M_{s_1}:\mathrm{Lin}(\mathcal{H}(d^{n}),\mathcal{H}(d^{k_1})), \\ &\quad M_{s_1,s_2}:\mathrm{Lin}(\mathcal{H}(d^{n + k_1}),\mathcal{H}(d^{k_2})), \cdots, \\ &\quad M_{s_1,s_2,\cdots,s_c}:\mathrm{Lin}(\mathcal{H}(d^{n + k_{c-1}}), \mathbb{C})\}. \end{aligned} Here the parameter satisifed k_1 = \min\{n,k\}, k_2 = \min\{n+k_1,k\},\cdots,k_{c-1} = \min\{n+k_{c-2},k\}. The POVM operator \{F_{\mathbf{s}}\} belongs to the linear space \mathrm{Lin}(\mathcal{H}(d^{cn})). When k = (c-1)\cdot n, we have k_1 = n,k_2 = 2n,\cdots,k_{c-1} = (c-1)n. This means that the last POVM operator supports on the whole linear space M_{s_1,s_2,\cdots,s_c}:\mathrm{Lin}(\mathcal{H}(d^{cn}), \mathbb{C}). Thus, the round-POVM operators \{F_s\} cover the whole space \mathrm{Lin}(\mathcal{H}(d^{cn})) and are equivalent to first storing c-copies of n-qudit states followed by c-copies collective measurements. If k < (c-1)n, \{F_s\} is restricted which we denoted as the set \mathcal{M}_{c,n}^{k}. We show that every element of \mathcal{M}_{c,n}^{k} can be realized by rank-1 POVMs within \mathcal{M}_{c,n}^{k} and post coarse-graining of the measurement results. Thus, it is sufficient to lower bounding all the rank-1 \mathcal{M}_{c,n}^{k} POVMs \mathcal{M}_{c,n}^k = \{F_{j}:= 2^{cn}w_j|L_j\rangle\!\langle L_j|\}_{j}, with \sum_{j}F_j = \mathbb{I}(d^{cn}).

ImportantLemma

\{F_s\}_s \in \mathcal{M}_{c,n}^{k} has decomposition \{F_s:= d^{nc}\sum_{a_c}w_{s,a_c}|L_{s,a_c}\rangle\!\langle L_{s,a_c}|\}_s, where \ket{L_{s,a_c}} is a normalized MPS vector on c \cdot n qudits with at most d^{k_j} bond dimension.

NoteProof (Click to expand)

Proof. The operator F_s can be constructed from those M_s operators through the identity: \begin{align} \mathrm{tr}(\rho^{\otimes c} F_s) = \sum_{a_c \in [d^{n+k}]}\begin{quantikz}[row sep=0.1cm, column sep=0.1cm] \setwiretype{n}&&&\gate[2]{M_{s_1, s_2}}&\gate[1]{M_{s_1}\vphantom{M_{s_1}^\dagger}}\setwiretype{c}&\gate[1]{\rho}\setwiretype{q}&\gate[1]{M_{s_1}^\dagger}\gategroup[4,steps=6,style={dashed,rounded corners,inner sep=-1pt},label style={label position=below, yshift=0.65cm, xshift=-0.7cm}]{$\ket{L_{s,a_c}}$}&\gate[2]{M_{s_1, s_2}^\dagger}\setwiretype{c}\\ \setwiretype{n}&&\gate[2]{\cdots}\setwiretype{n}&\setwiretype{c}&\setwiretype{q}&\gate[1]{\rho}&&&\gate[2]{\cdots}\setwiretype{c}\\ \setwiretype{n}&\gate[2]{M_{s_1,\cdots,s_c}}&\setwiretype{c}&\setwiretype{q}&&\gate[1]{\cdot\!\!\cdot\!\!\cdot}&&&&\gate[2]{M_{s_1,\cdots,s_c}^\dagger}\setwiretype{c}\\ \lstick{$a_c$|\!|\!\!\!}\setwiretype{c}&&\setwiretype{q}&&&\gate[1]{\rho}&&&&&\setwiretype{c}&\rstick{\!\!\!|\!|$a_c$} \end{quantikz} \label{eq:tensor_network_MPS} \end{align} Here we use single line to indicate the d-dimensional bond and double line to indicate the k_j-dimensional bond. The restriction of such (c,k)-POVM operators, which we denoted as the set \mathcal{M}_{c,n}^{k}, is equivalent to state that \{F_s:= d^{nc}\sum_{a_c}w_{s,a_c}|L_{s,a_c}\rangle\!\langle L_{s,a_c}|\}_s with \ket{L_{s,a_c}} a normalized MPS vector on c \cdot n qudits with d^{k_j} bond dimension: \begin{align} &\ket{L_{s,a_c}} =\sum_{a_j\in [d^{k_j}]} \ket{L_{s,a_1}}\ket{L_{s,a_1,a_2}}\cdots \ket{L_{s,a_{c-2},a_{c-1}}}\ket{L_{s,a_{c-1},a_c}}, \text{~where~} \forall \ket{e} \in \mathcal{H}(d^n),\\ &\langle e|{L_{s,a_1}}\rangle := \langle e|M_{s_1}^{\dagger}|a_1\rangle,\quad \langle e|{L_{s,a_{j-1},a_{j}}}\rangle := \langle e,a_{j-1}|M_{s_1,\cdots,s_j}^{\dagger}|a_{j}\rangle,\forall j>1. \end{align} The trace-preserving condition \sum_{s_j} M^{\dagger}_{s_1,\cdots,s_j}M_{s_1,\cdots,s_j} = \mathbb{I}(d^n) now transformed into \begin{align} \sum_{a_j,s_j} \langle e|{L_{s,a_{j-1},a_{j}}}\rangle \langle {L_{s,a_{j-1},a_{j}}}|f\rangle &= \sum_{a_j}\langle e,a_{j-1}|M_{s_1,\cdots,s_j}^{\dagger}|a_{j}\rangle\langle a_{j}|M_{s_1,\cdots,s_j}|f,a_{j-1}\rangle\\ &=\sum_{s_j}\langle e,a_{j-1}|M_{s_1,\cdots,s_j}^{\dagger}M_{s_1,\cdots,s_j}|f,a_{j-1}\rangle = \delta_{e,f} \\ &\hspace{-5em}\Rightarrow \forall j = 1,\cdots,c,\quad \sum_{a_j,s_j} |{L_{s,a_{j-1},a_{j}}}\rangle \langle {L_{s,a_{j-1},a_{j}}}|= \mathbb{I}(d^n). \end{align} Thus, \mathcal{M}_{c,n}^k can be implemented through rank-1 MPS-POVMs \mathcal{M}_{c,n}^k = \{F_{j}:= 2^{cn}w_j|L_j\rangle\!\langle L_j|\}_{j=(s,a_c)}, with \sum_{j}F_j = \mathbb{I}(d^{cn}), followed by classical post-processing rule j=(s,a_c) \to s. ◻

Given a pure quantum state \ket{L} that supports on c identical quantum systems with subsystem S \subset \{1,\cdots,c\}. Define P^S as the tensor product of Pauli operator P on the subsystem s if s \in S otherwise identity. We say the Pauli operator P are \varepsilon-correlated on the subsystem if and only if |\bra{L} P^{S} \ket{L}|^2 \geq \varepsilon. For a 2^k-bonded MPS states \ket{L}, we show that the \varepsilon-correlated Pauli is only taking no more than \varepsilon^{-1}2^{-n + k} proportion within all possible Pauli operators, as rigorously stated in Lemma.

ImportantLemma

Define the average Pauli correlation on subsystem S \subset \{1,\cdots,c\} as \mathcal{P}(S):= 4^{-n}\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}_n} |\bra{L} P^{\otimes S} \ket{L}|^2. Then if \ket{L} is an MPS state with no more than 2^k bond dimension, we have \mathcal{P}(S) \leq 2^{-n + k}. In the special case |S| = 1, \mathcal{P}(S) \leq 2^{-n}.

NoteProof (Click to expand)

Proof. In the simplest case c = 2,d= 2, a MPS state with \leq 2^k bond dimension always has Schmidt decomposition \ket{L} = \sum_{a = 1}^{2^k} \sqrt{\lambda_a} \ket{\phi_a} \otimes \ket{\psi_a} with \sum_a \lambda_a = 1. Take P^{\{1,2\}} = P \otimes P,P^{\{1\}} = P \otimes \mathbb{I}_n, then \begin{align} \mathcal{P}(\{1,2\}) &= 2^{-2n}\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}_n} \left|\sum_{a,a'}\sqrt{\lambda_a\lambda_{a'}}\bra{\phi_a}P\ket{\phi_{a'}}\bra{\psi_a}P \ket{\psi_{a'}}\right|^2\notag\\ &\leq 2^{-2n}\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}_n} \left( \sum_{a,a'}\left|\sqrt{\lambda_a\lambda_{a'}}\bra{\phi_a}P\ket{\phi_{a'}}\right|^2\right)\cdot \left(\sum_{a,a'}\left|\bra{\psi_a}P \ket{\psi_{a'}}\right|^2\right) \notag\\ &\leq 2^{-2n + k}\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}_n} \sum_{a,a'}\lambda_a\lambda_{a'}\left|\bra{\phi_a}P\ket{\phi_{a'}}\right|^2 = 2^{-n + k} \sum_{a,a'}\lambda_a\lambda_{a'}\bra{\phi_a\phi_{a'}}\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}_n} 2^{-n}P \otimes P\ket{\phi_{a'}\phi_a}\notag\\ &=2^{-n + k} \sum_{a,a'}\lambda_a\lambda_{a'}\bra{\phi_a\phi_{a'}}\ket{\phi_{a}\phi_{a'}} =2^{-n + k},\\ \mathcal{P}(\{1\}) &= 2^{-2n}\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}_n} \left|\sum_{a,a'}\sqrt{\lambda_a\lambda_{a'}}\bra{\phi_a}P\ket{\phi_{a'}}\bra{\psi_a}\ket{\psi_{a'}}\right|^2 = 2^{-2n}\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}_n} \left|\sum_{a}{\lambda_a}\bra{\phi_a}P\ket{\phi_{a}}\right|^2 \notag\\ &=2^{-n} \sum_{a}{\lambda_a\lambda_{a'}}\bra{\phi_a\phi_{a'}}\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}_n} 2^{-n}P \otimes P\ket{\phi_{a}\phi_{a'}}= 2^{-n} \sum_{a}{\lambda_a\lambda_{a'}}\bra{\phi_a\phi_{a'}}\ket{\phi_{a'}\phi_{a}}\leq 2^{-n}. \end{align} This generalized to c>2 case by noticing that \ket{L} = \sum_{a = 1}^{2^k} \sqrt{\lambda_a} \ket{\phi_a} \otimes \ket{\psi_a} is satisfied for bipartition \{1,\cdots,l\} \cup \{l+1,c\}. Take l being the least on in set S. For special case |S| = 1, it is trivially the same as c = 2 case. For |S| \geq 2, the same procedure followed: \begin{align} \mathcal{P}(S) &= 2^{-2n}\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}_n} \left|\sum_{a,a'}\sqrt{\lambda_a\lambda_{a'}}\bra{\phi_a}P^{\{l\}}\ket{\phi_{a'}}\bra{\psi_a}P^{S - \{l\}} \ket{\psi_{a'}}\right|^2\leq 2^{-2n + k}\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}_n} \sum_{a,a'}\lambda_a\lambda_{a'}\left|\bra{\phi_a}P^{\{l\}}\ket{\phi_{a'}}\right|^2 \notag \\ &= 2^{-n + k} \sum_{a,a'}\lambda_a\lambda_{a'}\bra{\phi_a\phi_{a'}}\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}_n} 2^{-n}P^{\{l\}} \otimes P^{\{l\}}\ket{\phi_{a'}\phi_a}\leq 2^{-n + k} \sum_{a,a'}\lambda_a\lambda_{a'}=2^{-n + k}. \end{align} ◻

In the case of c =2, we also have the inequality below:

ImportantLemma

\begin{align} \max_{\{F_s\}_s \in \mathcal{M}^{k}_{2,n}} \sum_{s} \frac{\left[\mathrm{tr}(F_s \mathrm{SWAP}^{\otimes n})\right]^2}{\mathrm{tr}(F_s)} \leq 2^{k+n} \end{align}

NoteProof (Click to expand)

Proof. ◻

1.2 Locality Constraints

When the POVM elements are restricted to act locally on subsystems, additional structure can be exploited to strengthen lower bounds. Consider a system of n qubits where measurements are constrained to act on at most k-local subsets.

NoteDefinition (Local POVMs)

A POVM \{F_s\} is k-local if each element F_s can be written as F_s = F_s^{(A)} \otimes \mathbb{I}^{(\bar{A})} for some subset A \subseteq [n] with |A| \leq k.

The key insight is that k-local POVMs have limited ability to extract global correlations. For distinguishing states that differ primarily in their long-range entanglement structure, locality constraints impose fundamental limitations.

TipOpen Direction

Establishing tight lower bounds for k-local adaptive strategies in property testing remains an active area. The interplay between locality and adaptivity is not fully understood.

1.3 Magic (Non-Clifford) Constraints

Restricting measurements to the Clifford group (stabilizer operations) provides another natural constraint class. Stabilizer measurements cannot efficiently distinguish states that differ in their “magic” (non-stabilizerness) content.

NoteDefinition (Stabilizer POVMs)

A POVM \{F_s\} is a stabilizer POVM if each element F_s is proportional to a stabilizer state projector, i.e., F_s = w_s \ket{\phi_s}\bra{\phi_s} where \ket{\phi_s} is a stabilizer state.

For n-qubit systems, the stabilizer states form a discrete set of size 2^{O(n^2)}, which is exponentially smaller than the continuous Haar measure. This discreteness can be exploited:

  • Stabilizer POVMs have limited resolution for distinguishing states with high magic
  • The shadow norm for Pauli observables under Clifford measurements has known bounds
  • Connections to classical simulability: states indistinguishable by stabilizer POVMs can be classically simulated
TipOpen Direction

Quantifying the sample complexity gap between stabilizer and universal POVMs for specific property testing tasks is an important open problem with connections to quantum advantage.
